sanskrit: sumuhūrtam abhūd yuddhaṃ tatra me dānavaiḥ saha vaśībhūtāś ca me sarve bhūtale ca nipātitāḥ
english: For a brief moment there was battle between me and those demons; all of them were brought under my control and cast down upon the earth.

sanskrit: etat kāryaṃ mahābāho yenāhaṃ nāgamaṃ tadā śrutvaiva hāstinapuraṃ dyūtaṃ cāvinayotthitam
english: This was the task, O mighty-armed one, on account of which I did not come then — hearing even of it, to Hāstinapura, and of the gambling that arose from that act of impropriety.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca vāsudeva mahābāho vistareṇa mahāmate saubhasya vadham ācakṣva na hi tṛpyāmi kathyataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O Vāsudeva, O mighty-armed one, O great-minded one, describe to me in full detail the slaying of Saubha — I am not yet satisfied with what has been told.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca hataṃ śrutvā mahābāho mayā śrautaśravaṃ nṛpam upāyād bharataśreṣṭha śālvo dvāravatīṃ purīm
english: Vāsudeva said: Hearing that king Śrautaśrava had been slain by me, O mighty-armed one, O foremost of the Bhāratas, Śālva marched upon the city of Dvāravatī.

sanskrit: arundhat tāṃ suduṣṭātmā sarvataḥ pāṇḍunandana śālvo vaihāyasaṃ cāpi tat puraṃ vyūhya viṣṭhitaḥ
english: That exceedingly wicked soul Śālva besieged it on all sides, O son of Pāṇḍu; he arrayed his forces and took position, keeping that aerial city ready at hand.

sanskrit: tatrastho 'tha mahīpālo yodhayām āsa tāṃ purīm abhisāreṇa sarveṇa tatra yuddham avartata
english: Stationed there, that king assailed the city with his entire advancing force, and battle raged at that place.

sanskrit: purī samantād vihitā sapatākā satoraṇā sacakrā sahuḍā caiva sayantrakhanakā tathā
english: The city was fully equipped on all sides — with banners and arched gateways, with wheels and palisade-stakes, with catapults and trenches.

sanskrit: sopatalpapratolīkā sāṭṭāṭṭālakagopurā sakacagrahaṇī caiva solkālātāvapothikā
english: It had platforms and covered ways, lofty watch-towers and gate-towers, devices for seizing hair and scalps, fire-brands, fire-tubes, and pestles.

sanskrit: soṣṭrikā bharataśreṣṭha sabherīpaṇavānakā samittṛṇakuśā rājan saśataghnīkalāṅgalā
english: It had corner-fortifications, O foremost of the Bhāratas, kettledrums and tabors, stores of fuel, grass and kuśa-grass, O king, along with śataghni-engines and plowshares.

sanskrit: sabhuśuṇḍyaśmalaguḍā sāyudhā saparaśvadhā lohacarmavatī cāpi sāgniḥ sahuḍaśṛṅgikā
english: It had bhuśuṇḍī-tubes, stone balls and clubs, all manner of weapons and axes, iron shields, and also fire and stakes with iron tips.

sanskrit: śāstradṛṣṭena vidhinā saṃyuktā bharatarṣabha dravyair anekair vividhair gadasāmboddhavādibhiḥ
english: It was furnished, O bull of the Bhāratas, in accordance with the rules prescribed by the treatises, with many diverse materials — clubs and other offensive implements in abundance.

sanskrit: puruṣaiḥ kuruśārdūla samarthaiḥ pratibādhane abhikhyātakulair vīrair dṛṣṭavīryaiś ca saṃyuge
english: It was manned, O tiger of the Kurus, by warriors capable of repelling attack — heroes of renowned lineages and of proven valor in battle.

sanskrit: madhyamena ca gulmena rakṣitā sārasaṃjñitā utkṣiptagulmaiś ca tathā hayaiś caiva padātibhiḥ
english: It was guarded by the central contingent, known as the Sārasa, and likewise by raised detachments, by cavalry, and by foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: āghoṣitaṃ ca nagare na pātavyā sureti ha pramādaṃ parirakṣadbhir ugrasenoddhavādibhiḥ
english: A proclamation was made throughout the city that wine must not be drunk, and those guarding against negligence — Ugrasena, Uddhava and others — were on full alert.

sanskrit: pramatteṣv abhighātaṃ hi kuryāc chālvo narādhipaḥ iti kṛtvāpramattās te sarve vṛṣṇyandhakāḥ sthitāḥ
english: "For Śālva, king of men, will strike when men are heedless" — with this in mind, all those Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas stood vigilant.

sanskrit: ānartāś ca tathā sarve naṭanartakagāyanāḥ bahir vivāsitāḥ sarve rakṣadbhir vittasaṃcayān
english: And all the Ānartas — actors, dancers, and singers — were all expelled outside the city by those who were protecting the accumulated wealth.

sanskrit: saṃkramā bheditāḥ sarve nāvaś ca pratiṣedhitāḥ parikhāś cāpi kauravya kīlaiḥ sunicitāḥ kṛtāḥ
english: All the bridges were broken, boats were prohibited, and the moats too, O Kauravya, were made well-staked with iron spikes.

sanskrit: udapānāḥ kuruśreṣṭha tathaivāpy ambarīṣakāḥ samantāt krośamātraṃ ca kāritā viṣamā ca bhūḥ
english: The wells, O best of the Kurus, and likewise the cooking pits, were secured; and for a distance of a krośa all around, the ground was made uneven and difficult.

sanskrit: prakṛtyā viṣamaṃ durgaṃ prakṛtyā ca surakṣitam prakṛtyā cāyudhopetaṃ viśeṣeṇa tadānagha
english: Naturally difficult of access, naturally well-guarded, naturally equipped with weapons — that fortress was especially so at that time, O sinless one.

sanskrit: surakṣitaṃ suguptaṃ ca sarvāyudhasamanvitam tat puraṃ bharataśreṣṭha yathendrabhavanaṃ tathā
english: Well defended and well concealed, furnished with all weapons, that city, O foremost of the Bhāratas, was like the abode of Indra itself.

sanskrit: na cāmudro 'bhiniryāti na cāmudraḥ praveśyate vṛṣṇyandhakapure rājaṃs tadā saubhasamāgame
english: None without a seal could go out, and none without a seal could enter the city of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, O king, at that time when Saubha had arrived.

sanskrit: anu rathyāsu sarvāsu catvareṣu ca kaurava balaṃ babhūva rājendra prabhūtagajavājimat
english: Along all the streets and at every crossroads, O Kaurava, O king of kings, there was a force, abundant in elephants and horses.

sanskrit: dattavetanabhaktaṃ ca dattāyudhaparicchadam kṛtāpadānaṃ ca tadā balam āsīn mahābhuja
english: That army, O mighty-armed one, had been given their wages and provisions, had been furnished with weapons and equipment, and had already proven their valor.

sanskrit: na kupyavetanī kaś cin na cātikrāntavetanī nānugrahabhṛtaḥ kaś cin na cādṛṣṭaparākramaḥ
english: Not one received an unjust wage, not one had wages delayed, not one was kept merely by patronage, and not one was of unproven valor.

sanskrit: evaṃ suvihitā rājan dvārakā bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ āhukena suguptā ca rājñā rājīvalocana
english: Thus, O king, Dvārakā was excellently provided for by the liberal-handed ones, and well protected by king Āhuka, O lotus-eyed one.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca tāṃ tūpayātvā rājendra śālvaḥ saubhapatis tadā prabhūtanaranāgena balenopaviveśa ha
english: Vāsudeva said: Having approached that city, O king of kings, Śālva the lord of Saubha then encamped with his large force of men and elephants.

sanskrit: same niviṣṭā sā senā prabhūtasalilāśaye caturaṅgabalopetā śālvarājābhipālitā
english: That army, endowed with the four divisions of force, protected by king Śālva, encamped on level ground near an abundant water source.

sanskrit: varjayitvā śmaśānāni devatāyatanāni ca valmīkāṃś caiva caityāṃś ca tanniviṣṭam abhūd balam
english: Avoiding cremation grounds, temples of the gods, ant-hills, and sacred trees, that army encamped.

sanskrit: anīkānāṃ vibhāgena panthānaḥ ṣaṭ kṛtābhavan pravaṇā nava caivāsañ śālvasya śibire nṛpa
english: By the division of the regiments, six roads were made, and there were nine descending passages in Śālva's camp, O king.

sanskrit: sarvāyudhasamopetaṃ sarvaśastraviśāradam rathanāgāśvakalilaṃ padātidhvajasaṃkulam
english: Fully furnished with all weapons, skilled in all arms, crowded with chariots, elephants, and horses, swarming with foot-soldiers and banners —

sanskrit: tuṣṭapuṣṭajanopetaṃ vīralakṣaṇalakṣitam vicitradhvajasaṃnāhaṃ vicitrarathakārmukam
english: Filled with contented and well-fed men, marked by the signs of heroes, with diverse banners and armor, with diverse chariots and bows —

sanskrit: saṃniveśya ca kauravya dvārakāyāṃ nararṣabha abhisārayām āsa tadā vegena patagendravat
english: Having thus encamped before Dvārakā, O Kauravya, O bull among men, he then launched his assault with the speed of the king of birds.

sanskrit: tadāpatantaṃ saṃdṛśya balaṃ śālvapates tadā niryāya yodhayām āsuḥ kumārā vṛṣṇinandanāḥ
english: Seeing that army of Śālva's lord descending upon them, the young princes, sons of the Vṛṣṇis, sallied forth and fought.

sanskrit: asahanto 'bhiyānaṃ tac chālvarājasya kaurava cārudeṣṇaś ca sāmbaś ca pradyumnaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: Unable to tolerate that advance of king Śālva, O Kauravya — Cārudeṣṇa and Sāmba and Pradyumna the great chariot-fighter.

sanskrit: te rathair daṃśitāḥ sarve vicitrābharaṇadhvajāḥ saṃsaktāḥ śālvarājasya bahubhir yodhapuṃgavaiḥ
english: All of them clad in armor on their chariots, with diverse ornaments and banners, they engaged in close combat with the many bull-like warriors of king Śālva.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā tu dhanuḥ sāmbaḥ śālvasya sacivaṃ raṇe yodhayām āsa saṃhṛṣṭaḥ kṣemavṛddhiṃ camūpatim
english: Taking up his bow, Sāmba, delighted, engaged in battle in that conflict with Śālva's minister, the army-commander Kṣemavṛddhi.

sanskrit: tasya bāṇamayaṃ varṣaṃ jāmbavatyāḥ suto mahat mumoca bharataśreṣṭha yathā varṣaṃ sahasradṛk
english: The son of Jāmbavatī released a great shower of arrows upon him, O foremost of the Bhāratas, as the thousand-eyed Indra releases rain.

sanskrit: tad bāṇavarṣaṃ tumulaṃ viṣehe sa camūpatiḥ kṣemavṛddhir mahārāja himavān iva niścalaḥ
english: That army-commander Kṣemavṛddhi endured that tumultuous shower of arrows, O great king, as immovable as the Himālaya.

sanskrit: tataḥ sāmbāya rājendra kṣemavṛddhir api sma ha mumoca māyāvihitaṃ śarajālaṃ mahattaram
english: Then Kṣemavṛddhi in turn released upon Sāmba, O king of kings, a far greater net of arrows wrought by illusion.

sanskrit: tato māyāmayaṃ jālaṃ māyayaiva vidārya saḥ sāmbaḥ śarasahasreṇa ratham asyābhyavarṣata
english: Then Sāmba, tearing apart that illusion-made net by illusion itself, rained down a thousand arrows upon his chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa viddhaḥ sāmbena kṣemavṛddhiś camūpatiḥ apāyāj javanair aśvaiḥ sāmbabāṇaprapīḍitaḥ
english: Then the army-commander Kṣemavṛddhi, pierced by Sāmba, fled on swift horses, sorely afflicted by Sāmba's arrows.

sanskrit: tasmin vipradrute krūre śālvasyātha camūpatau vegavān nāma daiteyaḥ sutaṃ me 'bhyadravad balī
english: When that fierce army-commander of Śālva had fled, a mighty Daitya named Vegavān then rushed upon my son.

sanskrit: abhipannas tu rājendra sāmbo vṛṣṇikulodvahaḥ vegaṃ vegavato rājaṃs tasthau vīro vidhārayan
english: Attacked by him, O king of kings, Sāmba the ornament of the Vṛṣṇi clan, O king, stood firm, the hero checking the speed of Vegavān.

sanskrit: sa vegavati kaunteya sāmbo vegavatīṃ gadām cikṣepa tarasā vīro vyāvidhya satyavikramaḥ
english: Then Sāmba, O son of Kuntī, the hero of true valor, swiftly hurled against Vegavān the swift mace, whirling it round.

sanskrit: tayā tv abhihato rājan vegavān apatad bhuvi vātarugṇa iva kṣuṇṇo jīrṇamūlo vanaspatiḥ
english: Struck by it, O king, Vegavān fell to the earth like a great tree with decayed roots, broken by the wind.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite vīre gadānunne mahāsure praviśya mahatīṃ senāṃ yodhayām āsa me sutaḥ
english: When that great demon had fallen, struck down by the mace, my son entered the great army and fought on.

sanskrit: cārudeṣṇena saṃsakto vivindhyo nāma dānavaḥ mahārathaḥ samājñāto mahārāja mahādhanuḥ
english: Engaged with Cārudeṣṇa was a Dānava named Vivindhya, recognized as a great chariot-fighter, O great king, a great archer.

sanskrit: tataḥ sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ cārudeṣṇavivindhyayoḥ vṛtravāsavayo rājan yathā pūrvaṃ tathābhavat
english: Then a most tumultuous battle between Cārudeṣṇa and Vivindhya took place, O king, just as the primeval battle between Vṛtra and Vāsava.

sanskrit: anyonyasyābhisaṃkruddhāv anyonyaṃ jaghnatuḥ śaraiḥ vinadantau mahārāja siṃhāv iva mahābalau
english: Both furious at one another, both roaring, they struck each other with arrows, O great king, like two mighty lions.

sanskrit: raukmiṇeyas tato bāṇam agnyarkopamavarcasam abhimantrya mahāstreṇa saṃdadhe śatrunāśanam
english: Then the son of Rukmiṇī took an arrow blazing like fire and sun, consecrated it with the great weapon-spell, and fitted it to the bow — the destroyer of enemies.

sanskrit: sa vivindhyāya sakrodhaḥ samāhūya mahārathaḥ cikṣepa me suto rājan sa gatāsur athāpatat
english: That great chariot-fighter, filled with rage, calling out to Vivindhya, hurled it — my son, O king — and Vivindhya fell lifeless.

sanskrit: vivindhyaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ ca vikṣobhitāṃ camūm kāmagena sa saubhena śālvaḥ punar upāgamat
english: Seeing Vivindhya slain and the army thrown into disorder, Śālva came again upon that place with the Saubha flying at will.

sanskrit: tato vyākulitaṃ sarvaṃ dvārakāvāsi tad balam dṛṣṭvā śālvaṃ mahābāho saubhasthaṃ pṛthivīgatam
english: Then the entire force dwelling in Dvārakā was thrown into confusion on seeing Śālva, O mighty-armed one, aboard the Saubha which had now descended to earth.

sanskrit: tato niryāya kaunteya vyavasthāpya ca tad balam ānartānāṃ mahārāja pradyumno vākyam abravīt
english: Then sallying forth, O son of Kuntī, and steadying that force of the Ānartas, Pradyumna spoke these words, O great king.

sanskrit: sarve bhavantas tiṣṭhantu sarve paśyantu māṃ yudhi nivārayantaṃ saṃgrāme balāt saubhaṃ sarājakam
english: "Let all of you stand firm; let all of you watch me in battle, as I repel by force the Saubha together with its king in this conflict."

sanskrit: ahaṃ saubhapateḥ senām āyasair bhujagair iva dhanurbhujavinirmuktaiḥ nāśayāmy adya yādavāḥ
english: "I shall today destroy the army of the lord of Saubha with iron shafts like serpents, released from the arm through the bow — O Yādavas!"

sanskrit: āśvasadhvaṃ na bhīḥ kāryā saubharāḍ adya naśyati mayābhipanno duṣṭātmā sasaubho vinaśiṣyati
english: "Take courage — there is no cause for fear. The lord of Saubha perishes today; attacked by me, that wicked soul shall be destroyed along with his Saubha."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati saṃhṛṣṭe pradyumne pāṇḍunandana viṣṭhitaṃ tad balaṃ vīra yuyudhe ca yathāsukham
english: While Pradyumna was thus speaking joyfully, O son of Pāṇḍu, that force stood firm, O hero, and fought with ease.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca evam uktvā raukmiṇeyo yādavān bharatarṣabha daṃśitair haribhir yuktaṃ ratham āsthāya kāñcanam
english: Vāsudeva said: Having spoken thus to the Yādavas, O bull of the Bhāratas, the son of Rukmiṇī mounted his golden chariot yoked with armored horses.

sanskrit: ucchritya makaraṃ ketuṃ vyāttānanam alaṃkṛtam utpatadbhir ivākāśaṃ tair hayair anvayāt parān
english: Raising his makara banner with its wide-open mouth and ornaments, he pursued the enemies with those horses that seemed to fly through the sky.

sanskrit: vikṣipan nādayaṃś cāpi dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ mahābalaḥ tūṇakhaḍgadharaḥ śūro baddhagodhāṅgulitravān
english: Brandishing and making resound his finest bow, the mighty hero, bearing quiver and sword, with leather guard and finger-bracer bound on —

sanskrit: sa vidyuccalitaṃ cāpaṃ viharan vai talāt talam mohayām āsa daiteyān sarvān saubhanivāsinaḥ
english: He, moving his bow with lightning speed from palm to palm, bewildered all the Daityas who dwelt in the Saubha.

sanskrit: nāsya vikṣipataś cāpaṃ saṃdadhānasya cāsakṛt antaraṃ dadṛśe kaś cin nighnataḥ śātravān raṇe
english: No one could find an opening against him as he repeatedly drew and released his bow, repeatedly slaying enemies in battle.

sanskrit: mukhasya varṇo na vikalpate 'sya; celuś ca gātrāṇi na cāpi tasya siṃhonnataṃ cāpy abhigarjato 'sya; śuśrāva loko 'dbhutarūpam agryam
english: His countenance showed no change; his limbs did not tremble; even as he roared like a lion, the world heard something wondrous and supreme.

sanskrit: jalecaraḥ kāñcanayaṣṭisaṃstho; vyāttānanaḥ sarvatimipramāthī vitrāsayan rājati vāhamukhye; śālvasya senāpramukhe dhvajāgryaḥ
english: The water-creature mounted on its golden pole — wide-mouthed, destroyer of all great fish — gleaming, terrifying, at the head of the chariot, his banner blazed at the forefront of Śālva's army.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa tūrṇaṃ niṣpatya pradyumnaḥ śatrukarśanaḥ śālvam evābhidudrāva vidhāsyan kalahaṃ nṛpa
english: Then Pradyumna, the afflicted of enemies, sallied forth swiftly and rushed straight at Śālva himself, intending to make war, O king.

sanskrit: abhiyānaṃ tu vīreṇa pradyumnena mahāhave nāmarṣayata saṃkruddhaḥ śālvaḥ kurukulodvaha
english: But the advance of the hero Pradyumna in that great battle was not tolerated by Śālva, who grew furious, O ornament of the Kuru clan.

sanskrit: sa roṣamadamatto vai kāmagād avaruhya ca pradyumnaṃ yodhayām āsa śālvaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: He, Śālva the conqueror of enemy cities, maddened with the intoxication of rage, descended from the sky-going vessel and engaged Pradyumna in battle.

sanskrit: tayoḥ sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ śālvavṛṣṇipravīrayoḥ sametā dadṛśur lokā balivāsavayor iva
english: The most tumultuous battle between those two champions — Śālva and the Vṛṣṇi hero — was witnessed by assembled people as if it were the battle between Bali and Vāsava.

sanskrit: tasya māyāmayo vīra ratho hemapariṣkṛtaḥ sadhvajaḥ sapatākaś ca sānukarṣaḥ satūṇavān
english: His chariot, O hero, was fashioned by illusion, adorned with gold, bearing a banner and a flag, with a trailing train, furnished with a quiver.

sanskrit: sa taṃ rathavaraṃ śrīmān samāruhya kila prabho mumoca bāṇān kauravya pradyumnāya mahābalaḥ
english: He, the glorious one of great might, mounted that excellent chariot, O lord, and released arrows upon Pradyumna, O Kauravya.

sanskrit: tato bāṇamayaṃ varṣaṃ vyasṛjat tarasā raṇe pradyumno bhujavegena śālvaṃ saṃmohayann iva
english: Then Pradyumna released a shower of arrows swiftly in battle, with the speed of his arm, as if bewildering Śālva.

sanskrit: sa tair abhihataḥ saṃkhye nāmarṣayata saubharāṭ śarān dīptāgnisaṃkāśān mumoca tanaye mama
english: The lord of Saubha, struck by those in battle, did not endure it, and released arrows resembling blazing fire upon my son.

sanskrit: sa śālvabāṇai rājendra viddho rukmiṇinandanaḥ mumoca bāṇaṃ tvarito marmabhedinam āhave
english: The son of Rukmiṇī, pierced by Śālva's arrows, O king of kings, swiftly released a vital-point-piercing arrow in battle.

sanskrit: tasya varma vibhidyāśu sa bāṇo matsuteritaḥ bibheda hṛdayaṃ patrī sa papāta mumoha ca
english: That feathered shaft sent by my son quickly split his armor and pierced his heart; he fell and lost consciousness.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite vīre śālvarāje vicetasi saṃprādravan dānavendrā dārayanto vasuṃdharām
english: When that hero, king Śālva, had fallen unconscious, the great Dānavas ran away, cleaving the earth asunder in their flight.

sanskrit: hāhākṛtam abhūt sainyaṃ śālvasya pṛthivīpate naṣṭasaṃjñe nipatite tadā saubhapatau nṛpa
english: A cry of lamentation arose from Śālva's army, O lord of the earth, O king, when the lord of Saubha had fallen insensible.

sanskrit: tata utthāya kauravya pratilabhya ca cetanām mumoca bāṇaṃ tarasā pradyumnāya mahābalaḥ
english: Then Śālva rose up, O Kauravya, and regaining consciousness, that mighty one swiftly released an arrow at Pradyumna.

sanskrit: tena viddho mahābāhuḥ pradyumnaḥ samare sthitaḥ jatrudeśe bhṛśaṃ vīro vyavāsīdad rathe tadā
english: Pierced by that arrow, the mighty-armed Pradyumna, standing in battle, the hero was sorely wounded in the collar-bone region and then sank down upon his chariot.

sanskrit: taṃ sa viddhvā mahārāja śālvo rukmiṇinandanam nanāda siṃhanādaṃ vai nādenāpūrayan mahīm
english: Having pierced him — the son of Rukmiṇī — O great king, Śālva roared a lion's roar, filling the earth with that sound.
